bss.topic: Formas de relevo: montanhas, planaltos, planícies e depressões

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que é relevo?
options: o conjunto das formas da superfície da Terra
a quantidade de chuva de um lugar
o tipo de vegetação de uma região
questions.answer: o conjunto das formas da superfície da Terra
questions.hint: Pense nas partes altas e baixas do terreno.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual forma de relevo é muito alta e tem encostas íngremes?
questions.hint: Escalar essa forma de relevo dá bastante trabalho.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como é uma planície?
options: um terreno plano e baixo, geralmente perto de rios ou do mar
um terreno muito alto e pontudo
um buraco no meio de montanhas
questions.answer: um terreno plano e baixo, geralmente perto de rios ou do mar
questions.hint: Pense em um lugar onde os rios deixam areia e barro.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como é um planalto?
options: um terreno elevado e com a parte de cima mais ou menos plana
um terreno abaixo do nível do mar
questions.answer: um terreno elevado e com a parte de cima mais ou menos plana
questions.hint: O nome junta 'plano' e 'alto'.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que é uma depressão no relevo?
options: uma área mais baixa que os terrenos ao seu redor
a montanha mais alta de um país
uma ilha no meio do mar
questions.answer: uma área mais baixa que os terrenos ao seu redor
questions.hint: Pense em algo afundado em relação ao que está em volta.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: A cidade de São Paulo fica em qual forma de relevo?
questions.hint: É um terreno alto e quase plano, bem acima do nível do mar.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual serra separa a cidade de São Paulo do litoral paulista?
questions.hint: Quem desce de São Paulo para a praia passa por ela.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Ao descer de São Paulo até Santos, o terreno vai...
options: do planalto até a planície do litoral
de uma montanha até outra montanha
questions.answer: do planalto até a planície do litoral
questions.hint: Santos fica à beira-mar, bem mais baixo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é o ponto mais alto do Brasil?
questions.hint: Fica no norte do Brasil, quase sempre coberto por nuvens.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O Pantanal é uma grande área plana e baixa que alaga na época das chuvas. Que forma de relevo ele é?
questions.hint: Terreno plano e baixo, onde a água se espalha.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes lugares fica em uma planície?
questions.hint: Procure o lugar mais baixo e plano.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em qual forma de relevo os rios costumam depositar areia e barro?
questions.hint: A água corre devagar em terrenos baixos e planos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que muitas cidades foram construídas em planícies e planaltos?
options: porque é mais fácil construir casas e estradas em terrenos planos
porque não existem rios nesses lugares
questions.answer: porque é mais fácil construir casas e estradas em terrenos planos
questions.hint: Pense em como seria construir uma rua numa encosta íngreme.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual frase compara corretamente o planalto e a planície?
options: os dois são planos, mas o planalto é mais alto
a planície é sempre mais alta que o planalto
questions.answer: os dois são planos, mas o planalto é mais alto
questions.hint: Lembre o que cada nome quer dizer.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Imagine que você vai de carro de São Paulo até a praia. Descreva como o relevo muda pelo caminho.
questions.hint: Use as palavras planalto, serra e planície.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que o relevo pode atrapalhar ou ajudar a construção de uma estrada? Dê um exemplo.
questions.hint: Pense em subidas, curvas e terrenos planos.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the main purpose of a procedural text?
options: to tell the reader how to do or make something
questions.answer: to tell the reader how to do or make something
questions.hint: Think of a recipe or a set of game rules.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is a procedural text?
options: a fairy tale about a dragon
questions.hint: Which one has steps to follow?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is written as an instruction (using an imperative verb)?
options: Pour the water into the jug.
The water was in the jug.
questions.answer: Pour the water into the jug.
questions.hint: Instructions usually start with a bossy verb.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which section usually comes first in a set of instructions?
options: a list of what you will need
a warning at the very end
questions.answer: a list of what you will need
questions.hint: You need to get everything ready before you start.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which adverb makes this instruction more precise? 'Stir the mixture ___ so it doesn't spill.'
questions.hint: Think about how you stir something without splashing it.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Find the adverb in this instruction: 'Carefully cut the paper along the dotted line.'
questions.hint: It tells you how to cut.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which instruction is the most precise?
options: Bake the cake for 25 minutes at 180°C.
Bake the cake for a while.
Put the cake in somewhere hot.
questions.answer: Bake the cake for 25 minutes at 180°C.
questions.hint: Look for exact numbers.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word is a time connective that helps put steps in order?
questions.hint: It tells you when to do something.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is a warning for the reader?
options: Be careful: the pan will be very hot!
questions.answer: Be careful: the pan will be very hot!
questions.hint: A warning helps keep the reader safe.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is a helpful tip?
options: Tip: wet your hands so the dough doesn't stick.
questions.answer: Tip: wet your hands so the dough doesn't stick.
questions.hint: A tip gives extra advice to make the task easier.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which adverb best completes this instruction? 'Hold the glass ___ with both hands.'
questions.hint: You don't want to drop it.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why are numbered steps useful in instructions?
options: they show the reader the order to do things
they tell the reader a story
questions.answer: they show the reader the order to do things
questions.hint: Think about what would happen if you did the steps in the wrong order.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which instruction is clearer for a reader?
options: Fold the paper in half from top to bottom.
questions.answer: Fold the paper in half from top to bottom.
questions.hint: A clear instruction says exactly what and how.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is the best title for a procedural text?
options: How to Plant a Sunflower Seed
questions.answer: How to Plant a Sunflower Seed
questions.hint: Procedural titles often start with 'How to'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Rewrite this instruction to make it more precise, adding an adverb and an exact amount: 'Add some water to the paint.'
questions.hint: Say how much water and how to add it.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write one tip or one warning for someone learning to ride a bike.
questions.hint: Think about what could go wrong or what makes it easier.

en_read.topic: Relationships in adventure fiction — 'Kensuke's Kingdom' (Michael Morpurgo)

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A "relationship" in a story is…
options: the way two characters feel about and treat each other
the place where the story happens
the last chapter of a book
questions.answer: the way two characters feel about and treat each other
questions.hint: Think about two characters together.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: When you "infer", you…
options: work out something the author has not said directly
copy a sentence from the text
questions.answer: work out something the author has not said directly
questions.hint: It is like being a detective.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: "Mia stamped past the old fisherman without saying hello." What can you infer about how Mia feels towards him?
options: she is unfriendly or cross with him
she is scared of the sea
questions.answer: she is unfriendly or cross with him
questions.hint: What does stamping and not saying hello show?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: "Every evening, the old keeper left a bowl of soup outside Ravi's tent, but he never stayed to talk." What does this suggest about the keeper?
options: he cares about Ravi but is shy or distant
he does not know Ravi is there
questions.answer: he cares about Ravi but is shy or distant
questions.hint: Think about the soup and the silence together.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which detail would be the best evidence that two characters have become friends?
options: One of them has a red hat.
questions.hint: Evidence must link to the relationship.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In Chapter 1 a girl refuses to share her food with a stranger. In Chapter 8 she cooks him dinner. This shows that their relationship has…
questions.hint: Compare the beginning with later.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Using evidence from several chapters helps you see how a relationship ___ over time. Write one word meaning "becomes different".
questions.hint: It is one of this week's keywords.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: "At first, Leo hid whenever the castaway came near. By the end of the summer, he waited on the beach for him every morning." Which word best describes the change in Leo?
questions.hint: Look at "At first" and "By the end".

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which phrase from a story is a time clue showing that a relationship has changed?
questions.hint: Look for a phrase about time passing.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: "The old man said nothing, but he moved over to make space for Kit on the rock." What can you infer?
options: he is starting to accept Kit
he wants Kit to fall in
he is too tired to talk
questions.answer: he is starting to accept Kit
questions.hint: Actions can speak louder than words.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In adventure stories, characters who are stranded together often become closer because…
options: they must rely on each other to survive
they live in the same street
they go to the same school
questions.answer: they must rely on each other to survive
questions.hint: Think about danger and teamwork.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: "Zara snatched the map and marched off alone." Later: "Zara handed Ben the map. 'You lead,' she said." What is the best inference?
questions.hint: Compare what she does with the map each time.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which sentence is the strongest way to begin an answer about how a relationship changes?
options: "At the start, the characters distrust each other, but later…"
questions.answer: "At the start, the characters distrust each other, but later…"
questions.hint: A good answer compares the beginning with later.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: "When the storm came, Sam held the rope tightly so that Grandpa Ott would not be swept away. Grandpa Ott had once called Sam 'a useless boy'." How has the relationship changed? Use evidence from both sentences.
questions.hint: Compare what Grandpa Ott once said with what Sam does now.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: "On the first day, the stranger shouted at Nell to leave his island. On the last day, he gave her his carved wooden turtle and turned away so she would not see his tears." What can you infer about his feelings for Nell at the end? Explain your evidence.
questions.hint: Think about the gift and the tears.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Think of two characters in a story you have read whose relationship changed. Explain how it changed, giving one piece of evidence from the beginning and one from later on.
questions.hint: Use "At first…" and "Later…".

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word is spelt correctly?
questions.hint: This person acts in plays and films.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: sail _ _ (a person who works on a ship)
questions.hint: This job ends in -or, not -er.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word means "a person who visits"?
questions.hint: Think of the -or suffix.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: doct _ _
questions.hint: You see this person when you are ill.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Add the suffix to the verb "direct" to make a word for the person who directs a film.
questions.hint: It ends in -or.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word means "a person who edits a newspaper or book"?
questions.hint: Add -or to "edit".

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: conduct _ _ (a person who leads an orchestra)
questions.hint: conduct + a two-letter suffix

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word means "a person who survives a disaster"?
questions.hint: Drop the e from "survive" before the suffix.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: instruct _ _ (a person who teaches a skill, such as swimming)
questions.hint: instruct + a two-letter suffix

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word ends with -er, NOT -or?
questions.hint: Most job words use -er; only some use -or.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which pair is spelt correctly?
questions.hint: One uses -or and one uses -er.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: "Survive" becomes "survivor". What happens to the final e?
questions.hint: Look at the letters after "surviv".

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Complete the sentence: The ___ shouted "Action!" and the cameras began to roll.
questions.hint: This person is in charge of making a film.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words.
questions.answer: directer → director; acter → actor; sailer → sailor; survivar → survivor; editer → editor
questions.hint: All five wrong words are jobs or people that should end in -or.
questions.text: The film directer asked a famous acter to play a brave sailer. In the story, an old doctor helps a lonely survivar escape from an island. A newspaper editer said it was the best film of the year.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which spelling of the word for a person who invents things is correct?
questions.hint: It uses the less common people suffix.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words, then check every job word ends correctly.
questions.answer: instructer → instructor; inventer → inventor; visiter → visitor; docter → doctor; conducter → conductor
questions.hint: Look for people words with the wrong ending.
questions.text: Our swimming instructer is also an inventer. He made a machine that helps every visiter float. Last week a docter and a train conducter came to watch our lesson at the pool. They both clapped loudly when my little brother finally swam all the way across without any help.

ipc.topic: Explorers and Adventurers: Zheng He and Columbus — voyages across oceans

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: A long journey by sea is called a…
questions.hint: It is one of this week's keywords.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which country did Zheng He come from?
questions.hint: He sailed for the Ming emperor.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: In which year did Columbus first cross the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.hint: It was at the end of the 1400s.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which ocean did Columbus cross on his first voyage?
questions.hint: It lies between Europe and the Americas.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which ocean did Zheng He's fleets cross to reach India, Arabia and East Africa?
questions.hint: This ocean is named after a country on its shore.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which country's king and queen paid for Columbus's first voyage?
questions.hint: He set sail from this country in 1492.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: How many ships did Columbus take on his first voyage?
questions.hint: Think of the Niña, the Pinta and the Santa María.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Zheng He led a series of great voyages. How many voyages did he lead?
questions.hint: It is the same as the number of days in a week.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which place did Columbus reach in 1492?
questions.hint: He landed on islands west of the Atlantic.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Where did Columbus believe he had arrived?
questions.hint: This is why he called the people he met "Indians".

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: How did Zheng He's fleet compare with Columbus's fleet?
questions.hint: Zheng He sailed with very large "treasure ships".

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which voyages happened first?
options: they happened at the same time
questions.hint: Zheng He sailed in the early 1400s.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: What is the word for the path that a ship follows from one place to another?
questions.hint: You can trace it on a map with a line.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which tool helped both explorers find their direction at sea?
questions.hint: Its needle points north.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Give one similarity and one difference between the voyages of Zheng He and Columbus.
questions.hint: Think about the size of the fleets, the oceans and what they were looking for.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Columbus's voyages changed life for the people already living in the Americas. Why is it important to think about their point of view too?
questions.hint: Think about who was there before the ships arrived.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A café has 3 kinds of bread and 4 kinds of filling. How many different sandwiches with one bread and one filling can be made?
questions.hint: Each bread can go with every filling.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A tree is 4 m tall. A tower is 3 times as tall. How tall is the tower in metres?
questions.hint: "3 times as tall" means multiply.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Each bike has 2 wheels. How many wheels are on 9 bikes?
questions.hint: One bike goes with 2 wheels.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Lily has 5 T-shirts and 3 pairs of shorts. How many different outfits of one T-shirt and one pair of shorts can she make?
questions.hint: Multiply the choices.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A pencil is 15 cm long. A ruler is 2 times as long. How long is the ruler in centimetres?
questions.hint: Double 15.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: There are 6 tables and each table has 4 chairs. How many chairs are there?
questions.hint: 1 table → 4 chairs.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A dog eats 3 tins of food a week. How many tins does it eat in 8 weeks?
questions.hint: Each week goes with 3 tins.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A tower is 36 m tall. It is 4 times as tall as a house. How tall is the house in metres?
questions.hint: Work backwards: divide.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: An ice-cream shop has 6 flavours and 2 kinds of cone. How many different single-scoop ice creams can be made?
questions.hint: Each flavour can go in each cone.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A recipe uses 2 eggs for every 1 cake. How many eggs are needed for 7 cakes?
questions.hint: 1 cake → 2 eggs.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Sam has 8 stickers. Ana has 5 times as many. How many stickers does Ana have?
questions.hint: Multiply by 5.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A menu has 4 starters, 3 main courses and 2 desserts. How many different 3-course meals can be made?
questions.hint: Multiply all three numbers.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A school has 7 classes. Each class needs 6 paintbrushes. Each paintbrush costs £2. How much do all the paintbrushes cost in pounds?
questions.hint: First find how many brushes, then the cost.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A bag of apples weighs 3 kg. A sack of potatoes is 6 times as heavy. What is the difference in weight between them, in kilograms?
questions.hint: Find the sack's weight first, then subtract.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Tom can make 20 outfits from some T-shirts and 4 pairs of trousers. How many T-shirts does he have?
questions.hint: What times 4 makes 20?

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Explain the difference between "3 more than 6" and "3 times as many as 6". Give the answer to each.
questions.hint: One means adding, the other means multiplying.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual destas palavras é um conectivo?
questions.hint: Conectivos ligam ideias ou frases.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Complete: "Eu queria brincar lá fora, ___ estava chovendo."
questions.hint: A segunda parte da frase mostra uma ideia contrária à primeira.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Complete: "Fiquei em casa ___ estava com febre."
questions.hint: A segunda parte explica o motivo.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Complete: "Lucas acordou cedo ___ tomou café com a avó."
questions.hint: Aqui só estamos somando duas ações.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Complete: "Começou a trovejar, ___ as crianças entraram correndo."
questions.hint: A segunda parte é a consequência da primeira.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual destas expressões é um marcador de tempo?
questions.hint: Ela responde à pergunta "quando?".

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual marcador de tempo combina melhor com o início de uma história?
questions.hint: Pense em como começam muitos contos.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual marcador de tempo indica o fim de uma sequência de acontecimentos?
questions.hint: Qual deles você usaria na última parte?

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Na frase "Primeiro, Ana lavou as mãos. Depois, ela cortou as frutas.", qual palavra mostra o segundo passo?
questions.hint: Procure a palavra que vem no começo da segunda frase.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual conectivo indica uma consequência?
questions.hint: Pense em "o que aconteceu por causa disso".

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Escreva a palavra que falta para ligar as frases mostrando oposição: "O cachorro é pequeno, ___ é muito corajoso." (use um conectivo de 3 letras)
questions.hint: É o mesmo conectivo de "queria, ___ não pude".

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual é a ordem certa dos marcadores de tempo numa narrativa?
options: Certo dia → Logo depois → No fim
No fim → Certo dia → Logo depois
Logo depois → No fim → Certo dia
questions.answer: Certo dia → Logo depois → No fim
questions.hint: Pense no começo, no meio e no final da história.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Por que usamos conectivos e marcadores de tempo num texto?
options: Para deixar o texto ligado e fácil de entender
Para deixar o texto mais curto
questions.answer: Para deixar o texto ligado e fácil de entender
questions.hint: A palavra "coesão" quer dizer que as partes do texto estão bem unidas.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual frase está mais bem ligada?
options: Choveu muito, por isso a rua alagou.
Choveu muito mas a rua alagou porque.
questions.answer: Choveu muito, por isso a rua alagou.
questions.hint: Leia cada frase em voz alta e veja qual faz sentido.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Reescreva juntando as frases com conectivos ou marcadores de tempo: "Pedro acordou. Pedro escovou os dentes. Pedro foi para a escola."
questions.hint: Você pode usar palavras como "depois", "em seguida" e "e", e trocar o nome repetido por "ele".

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Escreva três frases contando o seu fim de semana, usando pelo menos dois marcadores de tempo diferentes.
questions.hint: Use expressões como "no sábado", "depois", "à noite" ou "no domingo".

pt_leit.topic: Mitos indígenas: como a noite apareceu

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: O que é um mito?
options: Uma narrativa antiga que explica a origem de algo da natureza ou do mundo
Uma notícia de jornal sobre fatos de hoje
Uma carta enviada a um amigo
questions.answer: Uma narrativa antiga que explica a origem de algo da natureza ou do mundo
questions.hint: Pense nas histórias que contam como algo começou.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Como os mitos indígenas costumam passar de geração para geração?
options: Contados em voz alta pelos mais velhos
questions.answer: Contados em voz alta pelos mais velhos
questions.hint: Muitos povos indígenas guardam suas histórias pela tradição oral.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Um mito sobre "como a noite apareceu" quer explicar:
questions.hint: Olhe para o título.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Qual destas perguntas um mito poderia responder?
options: Qual é a capital do país?
questions.hint: Mitos explicam coisas da natureza.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Nos mitos, é comum que animais:
questions.hint: Pense em histórias com onças, jabutis e corujas que conversam.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Complete: os mitos indígenas fazem parte dos ___ dos povos indígenas, como conhecimentos sobre a natureza e sobre a vida.
questions.hint: A palavra está no objetivo desta semana: "valorizar os ___".

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Em um mito tupi muito conhecido, a noite estava guardada dentro de:
questions.hint: É algo que vem de uma palmeira da Amazônia.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Leia: "No começo, só existia o dia. Ninguém conseguia descansar." Qual problema o mito apresenta?
questions.hint: O que faltava para as pessoas descansarem?

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Leia: "Quando o pote se quebrou, os pedacinhos brilhantes subiram ao céu." O que esse trecho provavelmente explica?
questions.hint: O que brilha no céu à noite?

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Leia: "Desde aquele dia, a coruja fica acordada enquanto todos dormem." O que o mito explica nessa frase?
options: Por que a coruja é um animal da noite
Por que a coruja come frutas
Por que a coruja mora no rio
Por que a coruja tem penas
questions.answer: Por que a coruja é um animal da noite
questions.hint: Pense no hábito da coruja.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Muitos mitos terminam explicando algo que vemos até hoje. Qual expressão costuma aparecer nesses finais?
options: E é por isso que, até hoje...
questions.answer: E é por isso que, até hoje...
questions.hint: Procure a expressão que liga a história ao presente.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Qual atitude mostra respeito pelos saberes dos povos indígenas?
options: Ouvir as histórias com atenção e saber de qual povo elas vêm
Dizer que as histórias são bobas
Mudar a história e dizer que é igual à original
questions.answer: Ouvir as histórias com atenção e saber de qual povo elas vêm

books.subject: pt_leit
books.title: A Noite que Morava no Pote
books.premise: Toda tarde, Potira e o irmão Caué ouvem a avó Jupira contar, um pedaço por dia, uma história no jeito dos mitos: num tempo em que só existia o dia, a jovem Tainá, o tatu Bira e um beija-flor viajam até a Coruja Anciã para buscar a noite, guardada num pote de barro.

chapters.title: Capítulo 1: O tempo do sol sem fim
chapters.synopsis: Vó Jupira começa a contar aos netos um mito sobre um tempo em que não existia noite. Todos estavam cansados, até que o sábio da aldeia revelou onde a noite estava guardada.
chapters.text:
Toda tarde, depois da escola, Potira e o irmão Caué corriam para a varanda da avó Jupira. Ela morava perto do rio, numa casa cercada de mangueiras, e sabia muitas histórias. Naquele dia, ela avisou:
— Hoje vou começar um mito comprido. Ele explica como a noite apareceu. Vou contar um pedaço por dia.
Caué arregalou os olhos.
— Como assim, vó? A noite sempre existiu!
— Nem sempre, segundo esta história — sorriu a avó. E começou.
Há muito, muito tempo, numa aldeia à beira de um grande rio, só existia o dia. O sol nunca ia embora. As pessoas plantavam, pescavam e brincavam sem parar, porque não havia hora de descansar. Os olhos de todos ardiam. As crianças choravam de sono, mas a luz não deixava ninguém dormir.
Os animais também sofriam. O jabuti andava tão cansado que tropeçava nas próprias patas. A onça bocejava o tempo todo, e as flores murchavam debaixo de tanto calor.
Então o povo foi falar com o velho Araté, o mais sábio da aldeia. Ele ouviu com calma e disse:
— A noite existe. Mas ela está guardada num pote de barro, muito longe daqui, além das montanhas azuis. Quem cuida dela é a Coruja Anciã.
Todos ficaram em silêncio. Era uma viagem longa e perigosa.
Vó Jupira parou a história ali.
— E agora? Quem vai buscar a noite? — perguntou Potira, aflita.
— Isso fica para amanhã — respondeu a avó. — Mas pensem numa coisa: este mito tenta explicar algo que vemos todos os dias. O quê?
— Por que existe a noite! — disseram os dois juntos.
A avó concordou, e os netos foram jantar já imaginando o pote de barro.

chapters.title: Capítulo 2: Os três mensageiros
chapters.synopsis: No mito, a jovem Tainá, o tatu Bira e um beija-flor se oferecem para buscar a noite. Eles atravessam o grande rio com a ajuda do boto.
chapters.text:
No dia seguinte, Potira e Caué chegaram antes da hora. Vó Jupira riu, sentou na cadeira de balanço e continuou o mito.
Na aldeia, ninguém queria fazer a viagem até as montanhas azuis. Até que uma jovem chamada Tainá deu um passo à frente.
— Eu vou. Meus irmãos menores não conseguem dormir. Não aguento ver o sofrimento deles.
Logo depois, o tatu Bira saiu de um buraco no chão.
— Eu também vou. Sei cavar túneis, posso ser útil.
E um beija-flor, pequeno e rápido, parou no ar ao lado deles.
— Eu enxergo longe e voo depressa. Vou mostrar o caminho.
Assim, os três mensageiros partiram. Caminharam muito sob o sol forte, até chegarem ao grande rio. A água era larga e escura, e a correnteza era forte demais para nadar.
Tainá sentou na margem, desanimada. Então, do meio do rio, surgiu um boto cor-de-rosa.
— Por que vocês estão tristes? — perguntou ele.
Tainá explicou que precisavam buscar a noite. O boto pensou um pouco.
— Eu também gostaria de descansar. Subam nas minhas costas.
Tainá segurou firme, o tatu se enrolou como uma bola no colo dela, e o beija-flor voou bem perto. O boto nadou com cuidado, desviando dos troncos, até a outra margem.
— Obrigada, amigo! — disse Tainá. — Quando a noite chegar, ela será sua também.
Os três continuaram a viagem, felizes por terem vencido o primeiro desafio.
— Vó, por que o boto ajudou? — quis saber Caué.
— Porque nos mitos a natureza inteira está ligada — explicou a avó. — Pessoas, bichos, rios e plantas dependem uns dos outros. Muitos povos indígenas ensinam isso há muito tempo.

chapters.title: Capítulo 3: A floresta de espinhos
chapters.synopsis: Os mensageiros chegam a uma floresta cheia de espinhos que esconde o caminho. O beija-flor e o tatu trabalham juntos para que Tainá consiga passar.
chapters.text:
— Hoje tem perigo — anunciou vó Jupira, e os netos chegaram mais perto.
Depois do rio, Tainá, Bira e o beija-flor encontraram uma floresta diferente de todas. As árvores eram baixas e tortas, e os galhos estavam cobertos de espinhos compridos. Não havia trilha. Cada vez que Tainá tentava passar, os espinhos arranhavam seus braços.
— Assim não vamos chegar nunca — suspirou ela.
O beija-flor subiu bem alto, acima das copas.
— Lá do outro lado eu vejo as montanhas azuis! — gritou. — Mas, aqui embaixo, não vejo nenhum caminho.
O tatu Bira coçou a cabeça. Então teve uma ideia.
— Se não dá para passar por cima, vamos passar por baixo!
Ele começou a cavar. Cavou, cavou e cavou, abrindo um túnel debaixo das raízes. O problema é que, no escuro da terra, ele não sabia para que lado ir.
— Beija-flor, me guie! — pediu.
O beija-flor ficou voando no alto e, de tempos em tempos, descia até a boca do túnel.
— Mais para a direita! Agora em frente!
Tainá seguia engatinhando atrás do tatu. Demorou muito, mas, por fim, os três saíram do outro lado da floresta, cheios de terra e rindo de alegria.
— Sozinho eu teria me perdido — admitiu Bira.
— E eu não sei cavar — completou o beija-flor.
Tainá abraçou os dois amigos. As montanhas azuis já estavam bem perto.
Potira bateu palmas.
— Eles venceram porque se ajudaram!
— Exatamente — disse a avó. — Os mitos não explicam só a natureza. Eles também ensinam como devemos viver juntos.

chapters.title: Capítulo 4: A Coruja Anciã
chapters.synopsis: Os mensageiros chegam à caverna da Coruja Anciã e pedem a noite. Ela entrega o pote de barro, mas faz um aviso importante.
chapters.text:
Naquela tarde chovia, e vó Jupira contou a história na sala, com uma xícara de chá na mão.
Os três mensageiros subiram as montanhas azuis durante muito tempo. Lá no alto, encontraram uma caverna fresca e silenciosa. Dentro dela, sobre uma pedra lisa, estava a Coruja Anciã. Suas penas eram cinzentas como fumaça, e seus olhos amarelos brilhavam.
— Sei por que vieram — disse ela, antes que alguém falasse. — Vieram buscar a noite.
Tainá fez uma reverência.
— Sim, avó Coruja. Lá embaixo, ninguém consegue descansar. As crianças choram, os bichos tropeçam e as flores murcham.
A Coruja ficou um tempo calada, com os olhos meio fechados. Depois, apontou com a asa para um pote de barro, todo desenhado, tampado com uma folha de bananeira amarrada.
— A noite está aí dentro. Ela guarda o sono, o silêncio, o canto dos grilos e a luz fraquinha dos vaga-lumes. Eu a protegi por muito tempo, esperando que alguém pedisse com respeito.
Ela entregou o pote a Tainá, que o segurou com as duas mãos. Era leve, mas, lá dentro, parecia haver algo se mexendo.
— Escutem bem — continuou a Coruja. — Não abram o pote antes de chegar à aldeia. A noite precisa ser solta no lugar certo, com calma, para que todos estejam preparados.
— Prometemos — responderam os três.
O tatu Bira olhou para o pote com muita curiosidade, mas ficou quieto.
Caué cochichou para a irmã:
— Aposto que alguém vai abrir.
A avó fingiu não ouvir, mas sorriu.
— Repare, Caué: em muitos mitos, os mais velhos guardam um conhecimento precioso. E esse conhecimento é passado para quem pergunta com respeito.

chapters.title: Capítulo 5: O pote que cantava
chapters.synopsis: Na volta, o pote começa a fazer sons misteriosos. A curiosidade do tatu cresce até que ele desamarra a folha só um pouquinho.
chapters.text:
— Hoje vocês vão descobrir se o Caué tinha razão — disse a avó, e Caué esfregou as mãos.
Os mensageiros desceram as montanhas, felizes. Tainá carregava o pote com todo o cuidado. Mas, depois de algum tempo, um som estranho começou a sair lá de dentro.
Cri-cri-cri.
— Que barulho é esse? — perguntou o beija-flor.
— São os grilos da noite — lembrou Tainá. — A Coruja disse que estavam aí dentro.
Mais adiante, o pote fez outro som: um coaxar baixinho, como sapos perto de uma lagoa. Depois, um assobio suave, como vento entre as folhas. Era a música mais bonita que o tatu já tinha ouvido.
Quando pararam para descansar, Tainá deixou o pote no chão e foi beber água num riacho. O beija-flor foi procurar flores. Bira ficou sozinho com o pote.
— Só quero ouvir melhor — disse para si mesmo. — Não vou abrir. Só vou afrouxar um pouquinho a folha.
Com as unhas, ele desamarrou um dos nós. Na mesma hora, uma fumacinha escura escapou pela fresta e se espalhou em volta dele. O ar ficou fresco. O tatu sentiu os olhos pesados e bocejou.
— Que gostoso... — murmurou.
Mas a fumacinha não parava de sair. Ela se enrolava nas árvores, apagando as cores das folhas. Bira se assustou e tentou amarrar o nó de novo, mas suas patas tremiam.
— Tainá! Beija-flor! Socorro! — gritou.
Os dois voltaram correndo. Quando viram a fumaça escura, entenderam tudo.
Vó Jupira parou ali.
— Eu sabia! — disse Caué.
Potira, porém, estava com pena do tatu.
— Ele não fez por maldade, vó.
— Não — concordou a avó. — Mas às vezes a curiosidade sem cuidado traz problemas. E agora os três vão ter que resolver isso juntos.

chapters.title: Capítulo 6: Os cacos que viraram estrelas
chapters.synopsis: O pote cai e se quebra, e a noite se espalha por todo o céu. Os pedaços brilhantes sobem e viram estrelas, e o tatu, envergonhado, aprende a se esconder na terra.
chapters.text:
Vó Jupira apagou a luz da varanda antes de começar, e os netos riram, um pouco arrepiados.
Tainá correu para segurar o pote, mas tropeçou numa raiz. O pote voou de suas mãos, bateu numa pedra e se quebrou em muitos pedaços.
Então a noite saiu inteira. Uma escuridão enorme subiu, cobriu as árvores, cobriu o rio, cobriu as montanhas e se espalhou pelo céu inteiro. O sol, assustado, escondeu-se atrás do horizonte. Pela primeira vez, tudo ficou escuro.
Os três mensageiros tremeram. Não conseguiam enxergar nada.
— Estamos perdidos! — chorou Bira.
Mas Tainá respirou fundo e pediu calma.
— Esperem. Olhem para cima.
Os cacos do pote, que eram desenhados e brilhantes por dentro, começaram a flutuar. Subiram devagar, cada vez mais alto, até ficarem presos no céu escuro. Ali, viraram milhares de pontinhos de luz. Eram as primeiras estrelas.
Logo depois, os vaga-lumes saíram voando dos últimos pedacinhos, piscando entre as folhas. Os grilos e os sapos começaram a cantar.
— Que bonito... — sussurrou o beija-flor.
Com a luz das estrelas, eles encontraram o caminho. Mas Bira estava muito envergonhado. Cavou um buraco fundo e se enfiou nele, enrolado como uma bola.
— Eu quebrei a promessa. Não mereço ser visto.
Tainá se abaixou na beira do buraco.
— Você errou, mas também nos ajudou muito. Venha. Ainda precisamos levar a notícia à aldeia.
O tatu saiu, devagar, e seguiu com os amigos.
— E é por isso que, até hoje, o tatu vive cavando buracos e se enrola quando sente medo — disse a avó, acendendo a luz.
— E as estrelas são os cacos do pote! — completou Potira, encantada.

chapters.title: Capítulo 7: O primeiro amanhecer
chapters.synopsis: Os mensageiros voltam à aldeia, e todos dormem pela primeira vez. De manhã, o sol volta, e a Coruja combina que dia e noite vão se revezar.
chapters.text:
Era o último dia da história, e Potira e Caué trouxeram até um caderno para anotar.
Tainá, Bira e o beija-flor chegaram à aldeia guiados pelas estrelas. O povo estava assustado com a escuridão, mas Tainá explicou tudo: a viagem, a Coruja, o pote quebrado.
— Esta é a noite — disse ela. — Ela não é para dar medo. É para descansar.
Aos poucos, as pessoas deitaram nas redes. Os grilos cantavam, a brisa era fresca, e os vaga-lumes piscavam devagar. As crianças fecharam os olhos e, pela primeira vez, dormiram de verdade. Até a onça se enrolou e roncou. O boto, lá no rio, boiou em silêncio. As flores fecharam as pétalas para descansar.
Depois de muito tempo, uma luz rosada apareceu no céu. O sol voltava, devagar, sem pressa. Foi o primeiro amanhecer.
Então, do alto de uma árvore, ouviu-se uma voz conhecida. Era a Coruja Anciã.
— A noite fugiu antes do tempo — disse ela —, mas foi bem recebida. De agora em diante, o dia e a noite vão se revezar. Um trabalha enquanto o outro descansa.
— E a senhora? — perguntou Tainá.
— Eu vou ficar acordada à noite, cuidando de todos enquanto dormem.
E é por isso que, até hoje, a coruja é um animal da noite.
Vó Jupira fechou os olhos por um instante.
— Fim — disse.
Caué ficou pensativo.
— Vó, essa história é de qual povo?
— Esta é uma história que eu criei, do jeito dos mitos que ouvi a vida inteira — respondeu ela. — Os povos indígenas do Brasil têm muitos mitos de verdade sobre a origem da noite, e cada povo conta do seu jeito. Esses saberes são muito antigos e preciosos.
Potira escreveu no caderno: "Ouvir os mais velhos com respeito." E foi ver as estrelas.

books.title: The Keeper of Gull Rock
books.premise: Lost in the fog, ten-year-old Mila and her dog Pepper drift to a rocky island where a gruff old lighthouse keeper, Bram, wants nobody near him. Day by day, through storms, knots and card games, a wary standoff turns into a deep friendship that changes them both.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Off My Rock!
chapters.synopsis: Mila drifts through the fog in a small dinghy and lands on a rocky island, where an old man shouts at her to go away.
chapters.text:
The fog came down so quickly that Mila did not see it coming. One moment she was sitting in the little dinghy tied behind her uncle Joss's sailing boat, trailing her fingers in the water. The next moment the rope had slipped loose, the grey cloud had swallowed everything, and her uncle's voice was fading away behind her.
"Uncle Joss!" she shouted. Nobody answered except Pepper, her small scruffy dog, who whined and pressed against her legs.
Mila rowed until her arms ached. She had no idea which way she was going. After what felt like hours, the bottom of the dinghy scraped on stones, and a dark shape rose out of the mist. It was an island: a hump of black rock covered in seagulls, with a tall white lighthouse at the top.
She pulled the dinghy up the beach and climbed towards the lighthouse. Halfway there, a door banged open. An old man with a grey beard and a coat patched at both elbows stepped out and glared at her.
"Off my rock!" he barked. "Nobody comes here. Nobody."
"Please," said Mila, her voice shaking. "I'm lost. My boat drifted away from my uncle's."
The old man looked at her, then at Pepper, then out at the fog. For a long moment he said nothing. Then he pointed down the slope to a cave near the beach.
"You can stay in there until the fog lifts," he said. "But you keep away from my lighthouse." He went back inside and slammed the door.
Mila sat in the cold cave with Pepper on her lap, trying not to cry. When she woke up later, she found something by the entrance that had not been there before: a thick wool blanket, a bottle of water and two cooked fish wrapped in paper.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Line in the Sand
chapters.synopsis: The old man, Bram, draws a line Mila must not cross, but small gifts start passing between them.
chapters.text:
In the morning the fog was still thick. Mila found the old man on the beach, dragging a stick through the sand. He was drawing a long, straight line from the rocks to the water.
"My name is Bram," he said without looking up. "That side is yours. This side is mine. You don't cross the line."
"My name is Mila," she said, but he was already stomping back up the path.
For the whole day, Mila stayed on her side. She explored rock pools with Pepper, counted crabs and watched the old man. Bram did not seem to notice her, but she noticed him. He mended a fishing net, he talked quietly to the seagulls, and twice she saw him stop and rub his right knee as if it hurt.
At lunchtime, Mila looked down at the line. Right on Bram's side of it, there was a small bowl of hot soup with a spoon in it. Bram was nowhere to be seen.
Mila ate every drop. Then she had an idea. She searched the rock pools until she found the most beautiful shell on the beach: pink and curled, with a pearly shine inside. She placed it carefully on the line, right where the soup bowl had been, and wrote THANK YOU in the sand beside it.
That evening, when she came back from the rock pools, the shell had gone. In its place was a piece of driftwood. Someone had carved it into the shape of a little dog with a scruffy tail.
Mila held it up to Pepper. "Look," she whispered. "It's you."
High up in the lighthouse window, a curtain twitched. Mila waved. The curtain stayed still for a moment, and then, very slowly, a hand appeared and waved back.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: The Storm
chapters.synopsis: When a storm hits the island, Bram risks the rocks to rescue Pepper, and Mila is invited inside for the first time.
chapters.text:
On the third night, the wind began to howl. Waves crashed against the rocks and rain hammered the roof of the cave. Pepper hated thunder. At the first loud crack, he leapt out of Mila's arms and dashed into the darkness.
"Pepper! Come back!" Mila ran after him, but the rain stung her eyes and she could hardly see. Then a flash of lightning showed her something terrible. Pepper was trapped on a narrow ledge of rock at the edge of the sea, and the waves were getting higher.
Mila screamed his name. Suddenly a beam of light swept across the rocks. Bram was coming down from the lighthouse with a lantern and a coil of rope. He did not say a word. He tied the rope around a post, then lowered himself slowly towards the ledge, wincing every time his bad knee took his weight.
A huge wave rose up. Mila held her breath. When the spray cleared, Bram was climbing back up with Pepper tucked inside his coat.
He handed the shivering dog to Mila. Then he looked at her soaking clothes and her chattering teeth.
"You can't stay in that cave tonight," he said gruffly. "Come on."
For the first time, Mila crossed the line. Bram led her up the winding path and into the lighthouse kitchen. It was small and warm, with a stove glowing in the corner and shelves full of old books. He gave her a towel and a mug of hot chocolate, and he dried Pepper with a rough cloth, very gently.
"Thank you for saving him," Mila said.
Bram shrugged, but he did not look cross anymore. "A dog shouldn't be out in weather like this," he said. "Neither should a girl." Outside, the storm roared on, but inside the kitchen, it felt safe.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Knots and Cards
chapters.synopsis: Over the next days Bram teaches Mila about knots and tides, Mila teaches him a card game, and Bram shares a sad secret.
chapters.text:
After the storm, the line in the sand was never drawn again. The fog stayed, and so did Mila, but now she spent her days with Bram.
He taught her things she had never known. He showed her how to tie a bowline knot that would never slip, and a clove hitch for tying a boat to a post. He showed her how to read the tide by looking at the wet line on the rocks, and how to tell when the wind was about to change by watching the seagulls.
"You're quick," he said, when she tied a perfect bowline with her eyes closed. It was the first time he had praised her, and Mila's cheeks went warm.
In return, Mila taught Bram a card game called Snap, using an old pack she found in a drawer. At first he played very seriously, frowning at every card. But when Pepper jumped on the table and knocked the whole pile over, Bram threw back his head and laughed. It was a deep, rusty laugh, as if it had not been used for a very long time.
That evening, as the stove crackled, Mila asked him a question she had been wondering about for days. "Why do you live here all alone?"
Bram was quiet for a long time. Then he picked up a faded photograph from the shelf. It showed two young men standing beside a fishing boat, grinning.
"That's me and my brother, Ned," he said. "We had a terrible argument, years ago. About the boat, and money, and silly things. I came here to keep the light and I never went back. Never wrote to him either."
"Do you miss him?" Mila asked softly.
Bram put the photograph back carefully. "Every single day," he said.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: The Light Goes Out
chapters.synopsis: When the lighthouse lamp stops turning, Mila climbs up to fix it while Bram guides her, and he calls her his shipmate.
chapters.text:
One night, Mila woke to a strange silence. Usually she could hear the soft hum of the great lamp turning at the top of the lighthouse. Now there was nothing, and the windows were dark.
She found Bram at the bottom of the iron staircase, his face pale. "The lamp's stopped," he said. "There's a ship out there somewhere in this fog. Without the light, it could hit the rocks."
"Then let's fix it," said Mila.
Bram tried to climb the stairs, but his knee gave way on the tenth step and he sat down heavily. He shook his head. "I can't get up there. Not tonight."
Mila looked up at the spiral of steps disappearing into the darkness. Her heart was pounding. "Tell me what to do," she said. "I'll go."
Bram stared at her. Then he nodded and handed her a torch and a spanner. "The gear that turns the lamp has a chain," he said. "If the chain has slipped off, you need to lift it back over the teeth. Call down and tell me what you see."
Mila climbed and climbed, counting the steps to stay calm. At the top, the wind whistled through the gaps in the glass. She shone the torch on the machine. "The chain's hanging loose!" she shouted.
"Good girl," Bram's voice echoed up. "Loosen the bolt on the left, slide the chain over, then tighten it again. Slowly now."
Her fingers were cold and clumsy, but she did exactly as he said. With a clunk and a whirr, the great lamp began to turn. A beam of light swept out across the sea. Far away, a ship's horn sounded, low and grateful, as it turned away from the rocks.
When Mila came down, Bram was waiting with his arms open. He hugged her tightly. "Well done, shipmate," he said.

chapters.title: Chapter 6: A Sail on the Horizon
chapters.synopsis: The fog lifts and a boat appears, but Mila's joy turns to worry when she sees how sad Bram is.
chapters.text:
The next morning, the fog was gone at last. The sea sparkled, and for the first time Mila could see how far it stretched in every direction. Then she saw something that made her heart leap: a white sail, far away on the horizon.
"It's Uncle Joss!" she cried. "I know it is! I have to signal to him!"
She ran to tell Bram, but he was sitting on the bench outside the lighthouse, staring at the boat without smiling. He did not say anything at all.
"Aren't you pleased?" asked Mila.
"Of course," he said flatly. "You'll be going home." He stood up and went inside, and the door closed behind him with a soft click.
Mila stood very still. Suddenly she understood. When she left, Bram would be alone again, with only the seagulls to talk to. No card games. No one to teach knots to. No one to laugh with.
She went into the kitchen. Bram was polishing a brass lamp that was already shiny. "You could come with us," Mila said.
"This is my rock," he said, without turning round. "My place is here."
"But you'll be lonely!" Mila's voice came out louder than she meant. "You told me yourself you miss Ned every single day. You could write to him. You could do something!"
Bram put the lamp down. For a moment she thought he would shout at her, the way he had on the first day. Instead, he sighed and rubbed his eyes.
"You're right," he said quietly. "I've been hiding on this rock for too long."
He took a deep breath and picked up his old signal lamp. "Come on, then, shipmate. Let's get your uncle's attention." Together they climbed to the top of the lighthouse, and Bram flashed the light across the water: on, off, on, off. Far away, the white sail turned towards the island.

chapters.title: Chapter 7: The Promise
chapters.synopsis: Uncle Joss arrives, Mila and Bram say goodbye, and a letter months later shows how much Bram has changed.
chapters.text:
Uncle Joss leapt out of his boat before it had even touched the beach. He splashed through the shallow water and swept Mila into his arms.
"I've searched every island for miles," he said, his voice cracking. "I thought I'd lost you."
"Bram looked after me," said Mila, pulling her uncle up the beach. "He saved Pepper in the storm, and he taught me knots, and I fixed the lighthouse lamp!"
Uncle Joss turned to the old man and held out his hand. Bram hesitated, then shook it firmly. "She's a brave one," Bram said. "A proper shipmate."
It was time to go. Mila knelt down and opened her hand. Inside was the pink shell she had left on the line that very first day. Bram had kept it on his windowsill ever since, and that morning she had found it there.
"You keep it," Bram said, closing her fingers around it. "To remember the rock."
"Only if you promise something," Mila said. "Promise you'll write to Ned."
Bram looked out at the sea for a long moment. Then he nodded. "I promise."
As the boat sailed away, Mila waved until the lighthouse was just a white speck. Pepper barked one last goodbye.
Months later, back at home, a letter arrived with a stamp showing a lighthouse. Inside was a sheet of paper in large, careful handwriting.
"Dear Shipmate," it said. "I wrote to Ned. He wrote back. He is coming to visit the rock next summer, and he says he has a lot of card games to teach me. I have been practising Snap with the seagulls, but they are terrible at it. Thank you for crossing the line. Your friend, Bram."
At the bottom of the page was a drawing of a perfect bowline knot. Mila smiled and pinned it to her wall, right next to the little driftwood dog.
